subject: Urgent: Production 5xx/429 spike at Helix Therapeutics — immediate remediation plan
messages:
From: Support Helix <support@helixtx.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 5xx/429 spikes across API — urgent

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing a significant increase in 5xx and 429 responses from your API at ~15:50 PDT. Our frontend users are experiencing timeouts and the client is auto-retrying which is amplifying failures (we're seeing heavy retry amplification). Attached are a short log sample and a screenshot of our error-rate dashboard.

What we observe: 1) 5xx bursts (500/502) coincident with a jump in 429s; 2) per-request latency increasing from ~120ms to >800ms; 3) many requests timing out at our 10s client threshold.

This is impacting clinical workflows — we need an immediate remediation path and a timeline. Can we get a high-priority call now?

Attachments: helix_error_samples.log (text), prod_latency_series.png (screenshot)

Thanks,
Alex R.
Ops Lead — Helix Therapeutics
ops-contact@helixtx.com

Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spikes across API — urgent

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts.

We're escalating immediately. I've looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Marcus (SRE/runtime) for on-call triage; Rishi (AE) is copied for account comms. Marcus — could you please pull live traces (tailing request traces + node metrics) and confirm whether this is an autoscaling lag or node drain?

Immediate plan (short):
- Triage live traces + confirm pool saturation / GPU OOMs
- If Dedicated pool is saturated: emergency scale request + temporarily raise min replicas
- Apply request admission control (queue depth limit) and reduce client retries to avoid amplification
- Consider fallback routing to a smaller model variant for non-critical routes

Marissa — can you propose an immediate call window (next 30–45 min)? I'll notify execs depending on severity.

Sofia
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spikes across API — urgent

Quick update from infra: we see a sharp rise in GPU utilization across the Helix Dedicated pool starting 15:46 PDT. The pattern looks like: an increased concurrency of long-context requests + a scheduled nightly batch job from Helix that kicked off at 15:40 (per their logs) — the combination drove the pool to steady-state saturation.

Diagnostics (tailing):
- Node-level GPU utilization: several nodes > 98%
- Queue depth: spike to 2.5x typical, request latencies piling up (KV cache miss rate up)
- Autoscaler: triggered but lagged due to slow node provisioning (spot-preemption + cold-start)
- Error signatures: 500/502 from the runtime process indicating queue timeouts and transient worker failures; 429s correlated with admission control kicks.

Immediate mitigation recommendations (do now):
1) Force an emergency scale-up of the Dedicated pool (request +2x nodes from infra/ops quota) and temporarily increase pool min replicas so autoscaler doesn't scale to zero.
2) Apply an autoscale override (hold min for next 4 hours).
3) Push a routing rule to divert non-critical traffic to hosted multi-tenant pool (lower-cost model variant) — reduces upstream pressure.
4) Apply retry-suppression headers for Helix clients (instructions below) and add exponential jitter.
5) Warm caches by replaying a small set of representative requests to prime KV cache.

I'll start the scale action and open SUP-2048 to track the work. I'll also capture flame graphs and attach after the first collection.

— Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_node_flame_sample.txt (will follow)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: support@helixtx.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spikes across API — urgent

Alex — we can hop on a call at 16:50 PDT. Proposed agenda: 1) quick impact review (5m), 2) what we changed (10m), 3) immediate next steps and MAP (10m).

We've pre-populated an emergency mutual-action-plan and added a column for short-term credits & communication templates. Attaching: helix_map_emergency.xlsx (MAP stub).

On the call we'll cover: slowdown mitigation (traffic diversion), timeline for scale, and whether Helix can postpone or re-schedule any heavy batch jobs in the next 2–4 hours.

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: support@helixtx.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spikes across API — urgent

Alex — thanks for jumping on the call. Recap of immediate actions we executed during the call:
- Emergency scale: +80% capacity provisioned to your Dedicated pool; min replicas held for 4 hours (Marcus).
- Traffic diversion: non-critical routes routed to hosted multi-tenant variant to preserve throughput for critical endpoints (Marcus + Routing).
- Retries: we provided client-side retry guidance and enabled a server-side admission throttle for high burst traffic.
- Cache warmup: seeded representative prefixes to reduce cold-KV misses.
- Credits: we've proposed short-term usage credit while we stabilize (Marissa will share MAP).

Open items & next steps:
- Marcus to attach post-scale flamegraphs and trace snapshots (in SUP-2048).
- Marissa to send formal MAP and credits doc.
- Post-mortem scheduled for Mon 08/16 10:00 PDT (invite to follow) — exec-level attendees: Vivek and Lauren (for business impact).

We apologize for the disruption and will keep you updated as we complete validation.

Sofia

Attachments: none
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call status & follow-ups — SUP-2048

Post-call summary (collected metrics and remediation status):
- Error rate: 5xx/429 rates reduced to baseline within ~22 minutes after the emergency scale + diversion. Peak QPS reduced by ~45% for critical routes due to diversion.
- Latency: p95 fell from ~820ms to ~160ms after the KV cache warmed and additional nodes came up.
- Root cause hypothesis: concurrent heavy customer batch + high concurrency requests created a short window of sustained GPU saturation. Autoscaler responded but provisioning cold starts and spot preemptions introduced lag; queueing produced timeouts and worker failures.

Completed actions:
- Emergency pool scale and min-replica hold (done).
- Routing diversion to hosted fallback (done).
- Client retry guidance delivered to Helix (done).
- MAP & proposed credits sent by Marissa (see link).

Action items:
- Engineering: improve autoscaler cold-start latency (SUP-2048) — owner: Marcus — ETA: 2 weeks for a hot-instance pool and 6 weeks for broader autoscaler changes.
- Product: document recommended retry headers + example SDK patch (owner: Rishi) — ETA: 5 business days.
- CS: confirm credit amount and finalize comms (owner: Marissa) — ETA: 24 hours.
- Ops: review spot usage policy for Dedicated pools and offer an option for 'preempt-proof' nodes for high-SLA customers (owner: Vivek) — planning meeting Wed.

I'll attach the flamegraphs and traces to SUP-2048. If execs want a one-pager, I can produce a short blameless timeline for Monday.

— Marcus
Principal SRE

Attachments: prod_flamegraphs_15aug.txt (attached in jira SUP-2048)
